title.narrative: Improved Investment Climate within the Organization for the Harmonization of Business Laws in Africa (OHADA)

description.narrative: The objective of the Improved Investment Climate within the Organization for the Harmonization of Business Law in Africa (OHADA) Project is to strengthen OHADA's institutional capacity to support, in its member countries, selected aspects of investment climate reforms, including improved corporate financial reporting. There are three components to the project, the first component being institutional strengthening of the OHADA permanent secretariat and project implementation support. The objectives of this component are twofold: (1) to strengthen the institutional capacity of the Permanent Secretariat to enable it to discharge its institutional mandate by implementing critical recommendations of the 2009 operational and financial audits, and (2) to provide to the Permanent Secretariat the needed assistance to become an effective Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The second component is the Institutional Strengthening of the Joint Court of Justice and Arbitration (CCJA) and Regional Superior Magistrate School (ERSUMA). Finally, the third component is the improving corporate financial reporting.

To strengthen OHADA's institutional capacity and sustainability to support, in its member countries, selected aspects of investmentclimate reforms.The reason for the change is to include sustainability of the organization as a result of Project activities.The assumption is that strengthened OHADA institutions with additional capacity to elaborate, adopt and disseminate a new generation of investment climate reform regulations, enforce contracts, and provide fee based services to the private sector will contribute to improved investment climate in OHADA member countries and make the organization more sustainable. The assumption is also that the elaboration of norms, provision of tools and training will contribute to improved corporate financial reporting.

comment.narrative: <p>The Regional RCCM is operational and connected to several computerized national registries - Target 17 not-fully achieved with 13 countries connected before closing. However, it should be noted that the Covid-19 pandemic put this activity on hold for almost 2 years owing to travel restrictions for IT experts and sourcing problems for IT equipment.</p>

Indicator 3 Component 2: Number of Professionals trained by ERSUMA

comment.narrative:
<p>Number of Professionals trained by ERSUMA, Of which female - Target set at additional financing was 5,600 with 20% female. This objective was achieved and highly exceeded at 5,618 with 30% female.The school’s curriculum and courses were edited to make them more demand driven, and this established the basis for a training system, which is partly fee-based. Additionally, selected trainings were delivered as planned under the Project Appraisal Document. These activities were complemented by the development of a digital library as well as the strengthening of the research and documentation center with the acquisition of research equipment, including computers, books, and journals. ERSUMA organized virtual trainings including sixteen (16) webinars which was attended by 3,197 participants. These virtual trainings were organized and delivered using videoconferencing equipment funded by the project. Despite the positive progress, many ERSUMA-led activities were not launched or implemented on time including translation of some uniform acts and fundamental case laws into other OHADA languages.</p>
<p> </p>

PDO - Indicator 5: Percentage of Governments paying their dues on a regular basis

comment.narrative: <p>The final target was set ay 80 percent of member countries contributing to OHADA budget annually. It was only partially achievedat closing with 63 percent of member countries contributing. The organization still faces challenges to get members to contribute consistently. Inconsistency in recent years is attributed to Covid-19 and that several OHADA countries continue to face governance crises with a number of coup d'Etats recorded in West Africa. </p>
